scenarios.description: At the default wide viewport the home screen shows the drawn Constraint wordmark over a board tray with both avatars, Continue only when a game is saved, a Versus bot card with an Easy / Normal / Hard switch and Play, a Two players card with Play, a compact results strip with its reset, and How to Play and Settings; no mode or difficulty screen exists.

One tap on Play starts each mode from the home screen: Versus bot at the difficulty the switch shows (Normal at first) with seats You and Bot at that difficulty, and Two players with seats Player 1 and Player 2; a changed difficulty is still selected after a reload, and with a saved game the cards say that starting replaces it.

During a game the screen shows the board, a seat for each player (avatar, name, token mark, tokens left out of 8 and the score), the Match card with the last tile's art and names, and a top bar holding only the menu button; no log, status panel, legend or settings panel is present.

In a two-player game the seat to move is lit and labelled with its player's move while the other seat is dimmed, the board frame and the glowing tiles take the colour of the player to move, and after a take the lit seat, its label and the aria-live announcement switch to the other player. Player 1 sits left of the board and Player 2 right of it at the wide viewport; with motion on the flying Match tile never takes a tap.

With the page's randomness fixed so the player starts, only the 12 edge tiles glow; tapping an inner tile is refused with its reason, tapping an edge tile places the player's token there and the Match card shows that tile.

After the bot's take its cell is marked as the last move and a toast names the bot's take, exactly the tiles matching the last tile glow, a non-matching tile is refused with a reason naming both tiles, that refusal clears once the turn changes, and a matching take hands the turn back to the bot. With motion on, a tap right after the bot's take lands on the board.
With highlights turned off in the menu, no tile glows, a legal take still works and an illegal one is still refused with its reason; the setting survives a reload.

The How to Play dialog opens from the home screen and from the match menu, shows its pages (taking a matching tile, the opening, lines and squares, blockade and the full-board draw) with diagrams drawn with the tile art, closes with Escape or its close button, and returns focus to the button that opened it.
After a few takes the page is reloaded; Continue restores the same board, tokens, Match card, turn, mode and score of the sitting.

The test plays glowing takes in a bot game until it ends; the end screen names the result once (line, square, blockade or draw) with no end toast, the winning shape's cells are marked on the board, the seats show the won and lost expressions, and the results for that difficulty count one more game.

The test drives both seats of a two-player game with glowing takes until it ends; the end screen names the winning seat or the draw and how it happened, the score of the sitting counts it, and the results by difficulty are unchanged.

After a finished game the score of the sitting shows it; Play again keeps the score and swaps the starter, a second finished game adds to it, a reload with Continue in mid-game restores it, and leaving to the home screen and starting a game from it resets it to zero.
Play again after a finished game starts a new game in the same mode whose starting player is the other player.
Sound starts only after a user action, the mute setting in the menu survives a reload, and while muted no audio is played.

With the dark colour scheme emulated, on the home screen and in a game, the board, tiles, emblems, both players' tokens, both avatars, the material surfaces and the lit and dimmed seats stay distinguishable and all text meets a 4.5:1 contrast ratio.

With the light colour scheme emulated, on the home screen and in a game, all text, the seat labels on lit and dimmed seats and the play cards included, meets a 4.5:1 contrast ratio, and both players' tokens and avatars stay distinguishable.

At 390 x 844 the home screen (hero, Continue, both play cards, the results strip, How to Play and Settings) and the game (the board, both seats as nameplates at most 96 px tall with Player 2 above and Player 1 below, the Match card and the menu button) fit without horizontal scrolling, the game fits without any scrolling, and every tile and button is at least 44 px in both dimensions.
Using the keyboard only, the player changes the difficulty switch, starts a game in each mode from the home screen, opens and closes the menu and How to Play, and takes a legal tile.

With motion on, the avatars react to what just happened: the player to move is ready, the bot is thinking while it chooses, a player who takes nods, a refused tap makes that player wince, the waiting player glances at the other's take, and at the end the winner shows won with a bounce and the other lost; each reaction is read from data-reaction, and taps on the board still land while a reaction plays.

In a game at the wide viewport and at 390 x 844 the table shows its materials: a felt surface, a wood-grain tray, tiles with an edge and depth, bevelled tokens with their ring and diamond marks, and shaded avatars; no element on the page uses a blur filter or backdrop filter, and the page has no duplicate id attributes.
At the wide viewport and at 390 x 844, the bot's take toast and a refusal toast never overlap any board cell, and both still clear as before (the refusal when the turn changes).
